title: Minimum Operations to Equalize Binary String
summary: Given a binary string and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to convert all characters to '1' by flipping exactly k different indices.
statement: Given a binary string and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to convert all characters to '1' by flipping exactly k different indices. If conversion is impossible, return -1.
constraints: The binary string has length up to 100,000.
Every operation flips exactly k distinct positions.
Return the minimum operations or negative one when unreachable.
hints: Only the current number of zeros matters; flipping a zeros changes the count to current+k-2a.
BFS zero counts, visiting each reachable parity interval efficiently with next-unvisited disjoint sets.
Derive the legal low/high next counts, enumerate unvisited counts of that parity, and remove each once.
BFS gives minimum operations, and the interval derives from every feasible choice of zero versus one indices, so no transition is missed.
editorial: BFS gives minimum operations, and the interval derives from every feasible choice of zero versus one indices, so no transition is missed.

tests.explanation: Flip the sole zero in one operation.
Two carefully chosen three-index flips reach all ones.
